block.title: Homepage hero: fighter vs ark silhouette across a full bullet-sky
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 side-scrolling arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; flagship key art for a game homepage, ultra-detailed large-format art with clean vector shapes and pixel-art texture accents. The entire promise of the game in one horizontal sweep: on the far left, a steel-blue dart fighter with a bold blue hull stripe, cyan canopy and long orange engine ribbons flies hard right, trailing a tight fan of bright player-bullets, tiny against what fills the other two-thirds of the frame — the approaching broadside of a colossal mechanical fish-shaped fortress-ship, its riveted jaw-plates open like a harbor chain, throat-glow building deep inside as a dark red furnace light, rows of turret-pods and armor seams marching up out of frame top and bottom so the beast reads bigger than the canvas. Between them, the sky is a lattice: three crossing arcades of enemy fire — pink bead-streams, red orb fans and violet spiral wrecks, each bullet a bright core with a dark rim — and threaded single-handedly through the gaps, the fighter's thin counter-fire. Far background: a blue planet rim curving along the bottom edge studded with tiny dark fortress spires, stars above, one distant second manta-shaped wing silhouette climbing into the boss's shadow for scale. Everything saturated, outlined, legible at thumbnail size yet rewarding at full width. Deep-navy space, committed cyan-orange hero colors against the enemy's rust-violet mass, lifted shadows, never pure black. No text, no letters, no logo, no UI — leave the upper-left sky clean and quiet for headline type to be overlaid later.
